_doc: Per-weapon hold data sheets (WEAPON_HOLD_PROCESS.md section 2). Distances in metres along the weapon's shaft, from the back end (knob/butt) toward the working end. profile: [distance, radius] pairs of the weapon's outline (round weapons). primary: the hand that holds through the whole clip; support: the other hand (released where its fingers open or in release windows).

sledgehammer._note: Shaft = GLB +Y through grip_primary; distances from the butt (GLB y=-0.145). Profile = area-equivalent radius of the cross-section outline (convex hull) every 2 mm, simplified to 0.8 mm. The handle is oval, not round (rubber grip ~38 x 43 mm, wood ~27 x 30 mm). The head (from 0.703) is a 0.274 x 0.105 m block, so its profile radius (~0.095) is an area equivalent: it really reaches 0.137 m along the strike axis (GLB X) and only 0.0525 m across it (GLB Z). grip_radius 0.020 is the rubber grip at the primary hand; the support hand on the wood handle sees ~0.0147. Grips are the GLB grip empties (0.145 and 0.455 from the butt; GameGrip_R is the back one in the GLB, primary is Left to match the bat sheet). Hands-together alternative for the support hand: ~0.22.

crowbar._note: Shaft = GLB +Y through grip_primary; distances from the chisel tip (GLB y=-0.1997). Profile = area-equivalent radius of the cross-section outline (convex hull) every 2 mm, simplified to 0.8 mm. The shaft is an octagon 24.4 x 22.2 mm (corners at 14 mm). Above 0.58 the slices cut both the rising shaft and the returning claw arm, which sits ~0.05-0.09 m toward GLB -X, so the hook radii there are area equivalents of an off-axis shape (the hook reaches 0.097 m from the axis toward -X). Hit = the hook (0.58-0.70); the chisel end (0-0.06) is a second, butt-strike zone. One-handed: Left is the GLB secondary grip, used only for two-handed moves.

chainsaw._note: APPROXIMATION: a chainsaw is not a shaft. Shaft here = the saw's long axis, GLB +X through grip_primary (parallel to the bar); distances from the rear of the rear handle (GLB x=-0.080). Rear handle = primary (Right, always: chainsaws are right-hand-rear), front handle = secondary (Left), bar = hit zone. Known violations of the shaft model: (1) the rear grasp bar is tilted 14 deg above +X (right-hand grip axis [0.970, 0.242, 0]), so the hand-axis-vs-shaft gate fails by design; (2) the front grip is 0.152 m ABOVE this axis (GLB y) and the left hand grips across it (axis along GLB +Z), so the support-hand-on-shaft gate and weaponpath.py's shaft-through-both-fists assumption do not apply: the saw's orientation must come from the primary hand only (plus the support target at its true 3D offset [0.253, 0.152, 0] from grip_primary); (3) the profile is the area-equivalent radius of the whole saw's cross-section, centred on the axis, but the body's centre is ~0.03 m below it and the bar's centreline is 0.075 m below and 0.047 m to the right (+Z) of it, so use _capsules (GLB frame, metres) for collision. grip_radius 0.021 = rear grasp bar (44 x 31 mm); front handle tube r = 0.0142.
